_doc: The Lazarus Archive (UPDATE 11, T-190; docs/LAZARUS.md section 8; contract C7 in docs/U11_CONTRACTS.md). Each entry is an in-world document: Father Serafim's diary, one page per map in order (map00, map01, map02, map04a, map04b, map04c, map04d; the last page on the Moon), the Laboratory No. 4 files, the October 1944 Soviet front report, Reinholt's STAUB memos, Hale's sample order. body is plain text; its first paragraph is the reader's caption (what the object is), the rest is the document, as intel.json does. speaker_vo is the read-aloud line id (VO_SCRIPT section 27; Russian spoken, English subtitle). place_hint is words for the placement worker (T-200): where in the map it lies as a world prop through the story-props system, never an Easter egg step. order sorts the Archive's Lazarus shelf. Dates in Father Serafim's hand are Old Style (Julian, the Church's calendar); every Soviet and German document is New Style.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 1: Lazarus Saturday
entries.place_hint: The inn's cellar, on the lid of Helvetia cabinet 2 among the eight replacement units: a single leaf of ruled paper, Russian, in pencil, the edge burnt, lying where the Lost Requisition Crate's 'returned inventory' spills. It is not a Map 0 document and nobody at the inn could read it.
entries.body:
A single leaf torn from a ruled notebook, written in pencil in Russian in a careful, old-fashioned hand, one corner scorched. Translated.

Lazarus Saturday, the thirtieth of March.

They came at nine, in a truck, with a paper. I did not read it. Pyotr Ilyich read it to me, because I would not take it from the man's hand, and I am sorry for that now; it was a small thing to refuse and it changed nothing.

The bell. They put ropes on her at noon. She came down the last of the way on her own and cracked across the shoulder on the frozen ground, and the note she made I will hear until I die. At three they fired the tower. It fell across the graves.

Then they wanted the silver, and there is no silver, there has never been silver, and so they went down into the crypt. The lamp was lit. The young one in the good coat, Volkov they call him, read the words over the door aloud, and the others laughed, and he did not. He carried it up into the church in front of everyone. He broke the wax on the altar step with his pocket knife, to show them there was nothing in it.

There was. It was wet. It was red, not black. A thousand years, and red. It ran onto his glove and he wiped the glove on his coat, the way a man does.

I have the cloth it lay on. I am writing in the church because the church-house is theirs tonight. I kept the lamp forty years, as Father Ioann kept it before me, not to know, but to keep. Now I will keep this book instead.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 2: Palm Sunday
entries.place_hint: The Core Vault, at the foot of the Crucible's feed door under the brass plaque, among the returned inventory the vault's crate has shed: a second leaf of the same notebook.
entries.body:
The second leaf of the notebook, the same pencil, the same hand, a thumbprint of something dark on the margin. Translated.

Palm Sunday. No willows this year; nobody went for them.

Three of them are sick: the two who carried it up the stairs, and the one who caught Volkov's glove when he dropped it. The fever came in the night. They shake, and their teeth chatter, and they are thirsty past any thirst I have seen in a man. At first light the brigade left for Staryi Brod, the sick in the truck bed under a tarpaulin, Volkov in the cab with his satchel on his knees. He did not look at me. I think he wanted to.

Grach the feldsher and Avdotya Pakhomova sat with the sick all night in my kitchen, with wet cloths, because somebody had to, and they were the two who said so. I will remember that about them. I served the hours in the open church to eleven people.

The bell lies in the yard with her mouth in the mud. The children will not go near her, and I have not told them to.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 3: Great Wednesday
entries.place_hint: The pen hall, on top of the Helvetia cabinet that came north with the ballast, by the crane: a third leaf, damp, the pencil run.
entries.body:
The third leaf, the paper swollen with damp, the pencil run in two places. Translated.

Great Wednesday. Grach has the fever. Avdotya has it. The same thirst.

I have put them in the church-house where the others lay, and I sit with them, because now it is my turn to be the one who says so. Grach, between the shaking, gave me his instructions: boil everything, burn the cloths, let nobody else in. He is a good feldsher. He has been a good feldsher for thirty years for people who paid him in eggs.

A carter back from Staryi Brod says the three men died in the fever ward on Tuesday, and that there is a soldier on the hospital gate. He says typhus. When I told Grach, he said: typhus does not make you thirsty like this. Then he asked me what was in the vessel. I said I did not know. He said: you kept it forty years and you did not know? I said that was the whole of the keeping. He laughed, and it hurt him.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 4: Great Friday
entries.place_hint: Werk Thalbach, the Montage hall, under the Crucible's feed door: a fourth leaf, folded small, as if carried in a pocket.
entries.body:
The fourth leaf, folded twice and worn soft along the folds. Translated.

Great Friday. Grach died at four in the morning, and Avdotya an hour after, holding my hand so hard that I have the marks of it.

At noon a boy came over the fields from Staryi Brod, not by the road, because the road has soldiers on it now. He said that in the night the three dead men in the hospital got up. He said it the way a child says a thing he has seen, not a thing he has heard. He said they bit the orderly. He said the soldiers shot at them and they did not mind it.

I have not told the village. I have told them to stay in their houses, and they will, because it is Great Friday and they would have anyway.

Nobody will touch Grach and Avdotya. So I will. Tomorrow, under the tower, where the ground is already broken.

The fourth day. I keep coming back to the fourth day. I have read that chapter two hundred times, and never once from this side of it.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 5: Holy Saturday, and Pascha
entries.place_hint: The Kranich's bomb bay, on a casing rack among the stores that came aboard with the Helvetia crate: a fifth leaf, wedged under a strap.
entries.body:
The fifth leaf, written in two sittings; the second half in a steadier hand. Translated.

Holy Saturday. I buried them myself under the fallen tower, as deep as one old man can dig in a day, and read over them, and marked the place with two posts and a length of the bell's rope. Nobody came, and I do not blame them.

The road is closed. There is a cordon at the ford, with a machine gun and a board that says TYPHUS. The soldiers are boys. One of them called across the water to ask whether we had bread. We have.

Pascha. I served it at midnight in the roofless church, and the whole village came, every one, with candles, because the soldiers at the ford could not stop them and did not try. Christ is risen. I said it and they answered it, and I meant it, and I mean it now, writing this in the morning with the candles out. Whatever is in the vessel, and whatever lies in the ground under the tower, this is still true. I write that down so that I do not lose it.

The ground under the tower has not moved. It is the second day.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, page 6: Bright Monday, the fourth day
entries.place_hint: The Groom Lake hangar, on the lid of the British crate beside its manifest: a sixth leaf, the pencil pressed through the paper in places.
entries.body:
The sixth leaf, the pencil pressed hard enough to tear the paper in two places. Translated.

Bright Monday. The fourth day.

They came up a little after dark. I was in the church and I heard the rope posts fall. I will not write what they look like; whoever reads this will know, or will not need to.

I struck the bell where she lies, with the hammer from the smithy, because a bell is what the village knows to come to. And they came, running, to the church, and I shut the doors on the inside with the beam. Forty-one of us. The children are asleep on the vestment chests.

Grach and Avdotya walked round the church all night, slowly, the way the sick walk, and in the morning they were standing at the door and did not try it. They do not try doors. They wait. I know them both. Avdotya still has the kerchief I tied on her.

Lord, I buried them with my own hands and I said the words. The words were right. It is not the words that were wrong.

entries.title: Father Serafim's diary, the last page
entries.place_hint: Mondlicht, the fulfillment store, on the artifacts rack where the field units shelved one object from every market: the seventh leaf under a violet Darkmatter tag that reads 'Sol-3. Customer-generated. Do not reshelve.' On the back of the leaf, a list of names.
entries.body:
The seventh and last leaf, under a violet tag in Darkmatter's hand: SOL-3. CUSTOMER-GENERATED. DO NOT RESHELVE. On the back, in the same pencil, forty-one names in a column. Translated.

The eleventh. Three days in the church.

They will not come in. We can see the soldiers' fires on the rise at night, and they can see ours, and nobody crosses. A man with a megaphone said twice that the district is closed for typhus and that help is coming, and then the megaphone did not say anything more.

Nine have been bitten going for water. They are in the sanctuary behind the screen, and I sit with them, and Pyotr Ilyich keeps the count of the days on the wall in chalk, because the fourth day is the thing now, the only thing. Food for two more days. Oil in the lamp for one more night.

I have been thinking about the lamp. We kept it five hundred years and not one of us knew what for, and the ones who opened it were not wicked men. They were men with a paper and a truck, and it only needed that. It only ever needed that.

Whoever finds this: it was not the Lord who did this, and it was not that poor boy in the good coat either, not all of it. It was that nobody was left to keep watch. Keep watch.

I am going down to the crypt to fill the lamp, and after that I will open the church door myself, so that none of them has to be the one.

Remember, O Lord, Thy servant Serafim, and Matvei, and Avdotya, and all of them, by name. The names are on the back of this page.

entries.title: Report No. 1 on Object 'Lazar' (Volkov, May 1930)
entries.place_hint: Reinholt's laboratory in the Lab Wing, on the bench where the clerks laid out the Soviet satchels from the sealed wagons: a typed carbon in Russian with a German translation pinned to it in Reinholt's hand.
entries.body:
A typed carbon on thin Soviet paper, the heading of the OGPU's Operative-Chemical Section, a German translation pinned behind it in a woman's hand. The Russian original is stamped SECRET four times. Translated from the German.

To the Chief of the Operative-Chemical Section. REPORT No. 1 on Object 'LAZAR'. From: Plenipotentiary A. Volkov. 6 May 1930.

1. I opened it. I state this first so that it is not found out later. On 12.IV at the church of the former village of Chetverodnevo, in the course of the closure, I broke the seal of a vessel (lead sheath, glass, wax, cord) recovered from the crypt, in the belief that it contained nothing of value. It contained blood. The blood was liquid. I draw the Section's attention to the age attributed to the object by the local clergy (approx. one thousand years) and to the fact that the blood is still liquid today, 24 days later, in my custody, at room temperature.

2. Three members of the brigade who handled the object (Comrades Shestakov, Rudnev, Oleinik) fell ill on 13.IV with high fever and extreme thirst, and died in the district hospital at Staryi Brod on 15.IV. On the night of 18.IV, the fourth day, all three rose from the mortuary and attacked the staff. I was present. I report this in plain language because I have no other.

3. Everyone bitten died within three to five days and rose on the fourth day after death. The sequence held without exception in 41 cases observed by the cordon.

4. The village was liquidated by fire on 25.IV on my order under the typhus protocol. The settlement is to be removed from the district map. I recommend the file be kept separate from the typhus file.

5. The object is in a lead case in my custody. I have not slept well. I request that the Section take it. I request this knowing that the Section will not.

A. Volkov.

entries.title: Laboratory No. 4, vault inventory (November 1938)
entries.place_hint: Totenhafen, inside the warhead cage beside the lead coffins, in the consignment's paper sleeve: a single Russian sheet that travelled with Lazarusblut from Kaltenbrunn, with a German gloss.
entries.body:
A single typed sheet in Russian, folded into a German consignment sleeve, three signatures in the same hand one under another. Translated.

NKVD USSR. GUGB. LABORATORY No. 4 ('FOURTH DAY'). Vault inventory, 15 November 1938. Present: the Chief of Laboratory (Volkov), the Senior Technician (Osokina).

1. The vessel. Lead sheath, glass, wax (resealed 1930), cord. Contents: liquid. PRESENT.
2. Cultures, sealed, glass, in lead: LZR-01, 02, 03, 05, 06. PRESENT. LZR-04: NOT FOUND.
3. Exhibit 3: the priest's notebook (Chetverodnevo, April 1930; seven leaves). NOT FOUND.
4. Exhibit 4: the altar cloth. PRESENT.
5. Files 1 to 212. PRESENT.

NOTE. The box in which items 2 and 3 were kept was sealed by me on 2.IX.1938. The seal is intact. The lock is intact. The vault was not entered between 2.IX and today according to the register, which I keep. I have signed this inventory three times and it is still true. The Senior Technician, who has served here four years, asked me whether the notebook could have been misfiled. I have told her that I know where every page in this vault is, and that is not a thing I am proud of.

A. Volkov. A. Volkov. A. Volkov.

(In German, in pencil, at the foot, a different hand: 'Found with the Soviet material, Nov 44. Lot 04 is ours. How? R.')

entries.title: Laboratory No. 4, culture log (extract, 1936)
entries.place_hint: Groom Lake, the lab's long hall, on the specimen-room desk with Hale's programme papers: a photostat of Russian pages with an English translation typed between the lines.
entries.body:
A photostat of four ruled pages, the Russian handwriting faint, an English translation typed between the lines by someone at the range who did not finish it. Translated where the typing stops.

LABORATORY No. 4. Culture log, culture LZR-02. Keeper: Volkov. Extracts.

14.III.36. Rule 1. It lives in blood and in nothing else. Broth, serum, saline: dead in an hour. Whole blood: alive indefinitely. Dried on glass: dead. Frozen: not dead; waits.

2.IV.36. Rule 2. The fourth day. Subject 19 (see list) concluded 29.III, 03:10. Rose 1.IV, 03:00 to 03:20, within the hour. Not the third day. Not the fifth. Osokina calls it 'the calendar'. I have stopped correcting her.

30.V.36. Rule 3. The bite. A subject bitten by a risen subject takes the fever within a day and concludes within five. Not by air, not by touch, not by water, in our experience. By blood into blood.

18.VII.36. Rule 4. Direction. Voice: no. Light: no. Pain: no. The dog it knew: no. The man it knew, Subject 24's brother, brought in at Subject 24's own request before he concluded: no. It does not know a face. It goes toward the living and toward noise, and it is patient. I have written to the Directorate that it cannot be made to obey and I have been told to continue.

9.IX.36. Rule 5. Fire concludes it finally. Cold does nothing; a risen subject kept at minus twenty for eleven days walked when thawed.

21.X.36. Rule 6. There is one source. We have cultured from the vessel and from the risen and from the bitten and from the dust of the Chetverodnevo file, and every culture is the same culture, and none has ever been found anywhere we did not carry it. We have it. I would give a great deal to be able to say that sentence and believe it.

(Below, in the same hand, undated:) Subject 31 asked for a priest. Refused. Noted.

entries.title: Laboratory No. 4, subject list, transfer of 2 March 1937
entries.place_hint: The Bahnhof hut at Werk Thalbach, pinned beside the Kaltenbrunn transfer list: a Russian transfer list of sixteen names with a photograph of a hut, so that the two lists hang side by side. Shown with weight: paper, not people.
entries.body:
A transfer list with a camp's stamp at the head, sixteen lines, a ruled column at the right filled in by hand in dates; and a photograph, pinned under it, of a hut with sixteen bunks, fourteen of them stripped to the boards. Translated.

TRANSFER. From the camp administration to the disposal of NKVD GUGB Laboratory No. 4, 'for work of a special character', 16 (sixteen) persons, received 2 March 1937. Receiving officer: Volkov.

No. 4417 Abramov, Yuri Pavlovich, b. 1899 ... 6.III
No. 4420 Bekmuratov, Sabir, b. 1908 ... 6.III
No. 4431 Vilde, Augusts, b. 1891 ... 10.III
No. 4433 Gorenstein, Lev Moiseyevich, b. 1902 ... 10.III
No. 4440 Dudka, Ostap, b. 1911 ... 14.III
No. 4442 Yeliseyev, Pavel Pavlovich, b. 1896 ... 14.III
No. 4447 Zhuk, Taras, b. 1905 ... 18.III
No. 4451 Isakov, Nikolai, b. 1913 ... 18.III
No. 4458 Kalnins, Roberts, b. 1900 ... 22.III
No. 4460 Lomidze, Givi, b. 1909 ... 22.III
No. 4466 Matveyev-Lysenko, Ivan, b. 1898 ... 26.III
No. 4471 Nurgaliev, Farid, b. 1912 ... 26.III
No. 4473 Ostapchuk, Vasyl, b. 1904 ... 30.III
No. 4479 Pervushin, Arkady, b. 1907 ... 30.III
No. 4482 Sobol, Mordechai, b. 1894 ... —
No. 4486 Tikhonov, Yegor, b. 1915 ... —

The right-hand column is headed 'concluded'. The dates are four days apart from the ones before them. The last two are blank. On the back of the photograph, in pencil: 'Hut 2, 30.III.37. Two bunks made. Sobol and Tikhonov returned to the camp on my authority; the Directorate has been informed that the series is complete. If this is found I will answer for it. V.'

Under it, in German, in Reinholt's hand: 'Sixteen. I have a number like this of my own. I record them as a number because if I record them as men I will stop.'

entries.title: The order of last resort (1939)
entries.place_hint: Mondlicht, the Account, laid on the console beside the Terms of the Mark: the two orders on the Moon that nobody signed properly, side by side. A Russian sheet with a rectangle cut out of it.
entries.body:
A heavy typed sheet, the paper of a ministry, a rectangle the size of a signature cut cleanly out of the foot with a razor. Translated.

TOP SECRET. OF SPECIAL IMPORTANCE. ORDER. 20 June 1939.

Concerning the programme 'FOURTH DAY' (NKVD GUGB Laboratory No. 4).

1. The conclusion of the Laboratory is accepted: the agent 'Lazar' cannot be aimed. It can only be released.
2. The programme is suspended. The vessel and the cultures are to remain in the vault of Laboratory No. 4 under the personal responsibility of the Chief of Laboratory (Volkov), who is not to be transferred, arrested or otherwise removed without reference to the undersigned, for the reason that he alone knows how to keep it shut.
3. The agent is designated a means of LAST RESORT, to be employed only on the direct order of the highest authority, and only when the alternative is the loss of the state.
4. In the event of employment, the Chief of Laboratory will attend in person.
5. Nothing in this order is to be understood as approval of the work by which the conclusion in point 1 was reached.

(Signature cut out.)

In the margin, in pencil, in Volkov's hand: 'Point 2 is my life. Point 4 is my death. Point 5 is the only honest line on the page.'

entries.title: Front report, 30 October 1944: 'an epidemic among the enemy'
entries.place_hint: The stable yard, by the gate on the carters' road: a Red Army officer's dispatch case lying open in the snow beside a greatcoat, where a Soviet risen walked in from the east. A typed Russian report; on its back, a letter in pencil.
entries.body:
A Red Army dispatch case, the leather frozen stiff. Inside, one typed sheet in Russian; on its back, written in pencil in the field, a letter that was never sent. Both translated.

FRONT. COMBAT REPORT for 30 October 1944, rifle division (number struck through), to Army HQ.

1. In the course of 26–29.X the enemy's defence on the sector Point 112 collapsed. Enemy losses were heavy. Our units advanced 6 km and consolidated.
2. From 29.X an epidemic was observed among the enemy, with a high mortality. Our units did not engage the sick. Enemy dead observed moving in the open were engaged by fire where they approached our positions.
3. From 30.X isolated cases of an epidemic nature among our own personnel in the forward aid stations. Measures taken. Losses from disease: nil.
4. Morale of the troops: high.

Signed: Chief of Staff.

(On the back, pencil:)

Mitya. I am writing on the only paper I have, which is the lie I signed this morning, so you will know which one I mean.

They are our own. Point 3 is our own. I saw Sasha Kravets of the second battalion walk past the battery at dawn with the hole in him from Tuesday, and his boots gone, and he did not know me, and I have known him since Kursk. The ones from the aid station came out of the tent in the night in their bandages and walked west, past the guns, toward the Germans, and when the sentries shot them they kept walking, and when they fell they got up. The boys are calling them the Returned. The commissar has forbidden the word. The commissar has not been outside since Tuesday.

The special officer from Moscow who came with the strange shells on the 25th stood at the parapet this morning with his binoculars and did not lower them for an hour. His name is Volkov. He did not look like a man who was surprised. He looked like a man who had been waiting for a letter and had got it.

We are to say epidemic. I am saying it. If I do not come home, know that I did not become one of them by choice, and that none of them did, and that whoever you hear it from, it was not the Germans who did this to us first. Burn this. Your brother, Kolya.

entries.title: Memorandum: the wagons, Lazarusblut, the Heart (Reinholt, 9 Nov 1944)
entries.place_hint: Abteilung III's formulation rooms, pinned beside the gauges of the first dust mill behind the tonic vats: a typed memorandum with Reinholt's signature.
entries.body:
A typed memorandum on the Amt's paper, pinned beside a gauge dial with a violet dust on its glass, signed in ink. Translated.

PROJEKT WIEDERKEHR. Abt. I to the Director's file, copy Abt. II (Fasbender), Abt. III (Venner). 9 November 1944. Subject: the Soviet material.

1. Since 3.XI six sealed wagons have been received at the siding from the East Prussian front, containing enemy dead recovered after the events of 26–30.X, put down with fire at the front and re-sealed. Dr. Fasbender attended the first unloading and has asked not to attend another. His request is granted.

2. Cultures taken from the Soviet material are indistinguishable from the Lazarusblut cultured from our own raised miners in 1939 and held since. They are the same agent. I had believed for five years that the agent was a property of the stone. It is not. It is a sickness, and it was in the East before it was in our salt, and I do not know how it came to be in both. The Soviet file found with the material (see translation) suggests that they do not know either, and that they have known it longer.

3. Rate. In the East the agent waits four days. Here, in the Laboratory Wing, 300 m from the Heart, a dosed subject rose in forty minutes. In the Core Vault, Osterkamp's rabbit rose in under four. The nearer the stone, the less it waits. The stone does not raise; the stone answers.

4. Proposal. If the agent is ground with the stone to the fineness of the tonic concentrate, it will carry on the air as a dust, and a body that has breathed it carries both at once: it will rise in minutes when it dies, wherever it dies, and it will answer the Ledger's carrier like a marked man. Abt. III's mills are suitable with modification. Programme name: STAUB. Target: the source of the material, which is to say the East.

5. Personal note, to be removed from the copy for Berlin: I named it Lazarusblut in 1939 because a man four days dead came home and I wanted that for my daughter. I did not know the name was already right. Reinholt.

entries.title: Circular: the Marke, a second line (Abteilung III, 20 Nov 1944)
entries.place_hint: The Administration Block's notice board beside the Marke poster, a typed circular pinned over the poster's lower edge; below the old slogan a new line has been stencilled: SCHUTZ GEGEN DIE LAZARUSKRANKHEIT.
entries.body:
A typed circular pinned over the lower edge of the recruiting poster; under the old slogan a new line has been stencilled in violet. Translated.

ABT. III (FORMULIERUNG) to all unit commanders, Kaltenbrunn and the road garrisons. Circular 31/44, 20 November 1944. Subject: the Marke.

1. With immediate effect the Marke is issued to all personnel not yet carrying it, on application, without charge against pay. The poster's wording is amended: DIE MARKE, DIE DICH HÄLT. SCHUTZ GEGEN DIE LAZARUSKRANKHEIT. (The mark that keeps you. Protection against the Lazarus sickness.)

2. Commanders will explain to the men that the sickness carried west by the enemy's dead is now in the district, that the Marke places the carrier under the skin where the sickness can be held, and that a marked man who falls will be recovered. The words 'recovered' and 'held' are to be used. The word 'rise' is not.

3. Issue to the labour contingents: no. Issue to the Polish nursing staff: no.

4. Refusals are to be noted by name and forwarded to Security (Lenz). Venner.

In ink, at the foot, a careful hand: 'It is not protection. A marked man who dies gets up in minutes and goes where the line tells him. You have put the one thing the Russians could not do into a grain of glass and sold it as a cure. I refuse it again. F.'

Under that, in violet pencil: 'Noted. L.'

entries.title: STAUB, Einsatz 1: the release order and the weather note (19–20 Dec 1944)
entries.place_hint: The Generator Hall's weather board by the Hauptschalter, or the rocket pad's hut on the surface if T-192's set adds one: a typed order with a wind reading and a handwritten note clipped to it.
entries.body:
A typed order with a strip of weather-service tape glued to it and a note clipped over the tape in pencil. Translated.

PROJEKT WIEDERKEHR. ORDER: STAUB, EINSATZ 1. 19 December 1944.

1. On 20.XII at 22:00 six rockets, each with a STAUB canister (2.4 kg, lot S-1 to S-6), are to be fired from the pad above the Minehead Yard on bearing 085 at the enemy positions on the eastern front, range per Abt. II's tables.
2. Weather. Wetterdienst Breslau, 19.XII, 18:00: wind west, 15 km/h, steady through the night. Release approved on this forecast. A wind from the east cancels the release. Confirm at 21:30.
3. Dr. Reinholt will be in the Core Vault during the release for the parallel test. The Heart is not to be brought above 60 per cent. Lenz.

(The tape, 20.XII, 21:30: WIND W 12 KM/H. STEADY.)

(The note, pencil, 22:40, a shaking hand:) The vane has gone round. East, and freshening. All six are away. I have telephoned the vault. She says she is at full and will not come down. She says something said 'Mama'. The lights in Wilcza Góra have gone out. Then the inn road. Then ours. God forgive us, we aimed it at them. Brandauer.

entries.title: Directive LANTERN, amendment of 16 November 1944: the sample order
entries.place_hint: The Groom Lake hangar office, on Hale's desk beside the program log, where it can be read through the glass: a British Most Secret sheet with the Groom Lake receipt stamp.
entries.body:
A single British sheet, MOST SECRET, the Groom Lake receiving stamp across one corner in purple ink. Initialled H.

MOST SECRET. EYES ONLY. LT. M. ASHWORTH. DIRECTIVE LANTERN: AMENDMENT No. 1, 16 November 1944. Supersedes paragraph 1.

1. Primary objective: recover viable samples of
 (a) the material designated NACHTGLAS (see the 1943 Basel sample), and
 (b) the agent designated LAZARUS: the sickness reported in Soviet front traffic from October 1944 as 'an epidemic among the enemy', and in enemy documents as 'Lazarusblut'. Blood or tissue of the risen, sealed.
Secure both in the lead-lined containers provided, separately. Do not expose to living tissue. Retrieve the tokens (right hand or brow) as before; same container as (a). Do not ask the bearer.

2. Intelligence note. Moscow's own traffic shows the agent was released by Soviet forces and then turned on them. The Russians have had it longer than anyone. The Germans have it now and are doing something to it at the target facility. We have neither. The war will end. This will not. Priority over every other objective, Dr. Fasbender included.

3. Nothing in this amendment is to be shared with US personnel.

H.

(Below, in an American hand, pencil:) Received Groom Lake 14 April 1945 with the crate. Para. 3 noted with amusement. L.H.
